standard: Visible construction refinement acceptable at application scale; not a numerical quality score or release approval.

front.note: Three small tapered flames now read clearly above the original graduated pillars.

rear.note: Opposite view retains the three candle heights and shows pointed, gently bent flame tops.

detail.note: Full detail confirms closed teardrop flame silhouettes replace the blunt luminous cylinders; emission remains restrained.

underside.note: The three original wax bases stay closed and level.

clay.note: Material-free view confirms the pointed flame geometry; the candles remain intentionally simple and stylized.

front.note: The seat now has a continuous thin perimeter seam rather than exposed broken ends.

rear.note: Back mounts and cantilever runners retain their original connections while the seam follows the rear seat edge.

detail.note: The full front seam stays seated on the existing lofted cushion, with small cloth-following irregularity instead of floating wire.

underside.note: The closed seat pan and supported runner structure remain intact.

clay.note: The piping follows the upholstered form in clay without altering the chair silhouette.

front.note: The complete seat seam now joins all four sides beneath the original padded arms.

rear.note: Rear frame, arm supports and cushion attachments remain consistent.

detail.note: Full detail confirms a continuous seated line across both front corners; gentle waviness follows the retained cloth surface.

underside.note: The seat base and chrome cantilever legs remain closed and connected.

clay.note: The repaired seam and softened seat remain legible without color, preserving the original lounge-chair construction.

front.note: The oval top and round foot now have smooth radial silhouettes rather than polygonal steps.

rear.note: The opposite view preserves the original tapered pedestal and broad top proportions.

detail.note: Full detail shows continuous foot and tabletop curves while retaining the measured turned profile.

underside.note: The pedestal is visibly seated against the top; the original closed foot and underside remain complete.

clay.note: Smooth construction and a connected pedestal are visible in clay, improving the previously angular silhouette.

front.note: The alternating colors now share one continuous cloth surface instead of raised tile-like plates.

rear.note: Opposite view confirms there are no deep grid gaps between the checker squares.

detail.note: Full detail shows contiguous checks and small separated yarn fringes; the original backing remains comparatively thick.

underside.note: The closed backing is retained and all fringe groups stay attached along the two edges.

clay.note: Clay shows a continuous textile panel with yarn fringe, a clear construction improvement over individual beveled tiles.
